chunks: Yet they worship those apart from God who cannot provide for them any sustenance from the heavens or the earth, nor will they have power to do so.
ai.seo_question: Why do people worship false gods who cannot provide sustenance?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the logical inconsistency of directing worship to inert idols that lack even the basic capacity to provide sustenance (rizq), contrasting them with Allah’s absolute sovereignty. It serves as a foundational argument for Tawhid, emphasizing that true divinity requires the power of creation and provision, which false gods inherently lack. This critique extends beyond mere idolatry to include any entity elevated to divine status without independent agency.
